title: Lutherans are not Remonstrants on Christ's death: no free-will application, no salvation without knowing Christ
pass_a_gloss: Yet the Lutherans' account is not the same as the Remonstrants'. For they hold neither that the application of Christ's death and its fruit hang on the powers of free choice — powers that are none, original sin being asserted — nor that anyone can be saved by the force of a universal redemption without knowledge of Christ.
pass_b_english: Yet the Lutherans' case is not the Remonstrants' case.
They do not make the application of Christ's death and its fruit hang on the powers of free choice — powers that are none, once original sin is granted.
Nor do they allow that anyone can be saved by the force of a universal redemption without knowing Christ.
source_text: Nec tamen ratio eadem Lutheranorum est quae Remonstrant. Illi enim, nec applicationem Mortis Christi & fructum pendere à viribus Lib. Arbitrii, quae nullae sint, asserto Peccato Originis; nec vi Redempt. universalis salvari quemquam posse, sine cognitione Christi.
notes: Controv. print p. 53 / PDF ~154. Close of Controv. VII tip before VIII.

choices.why: liberum arbitrium as faculty/power, not modern free-will system slogan alone
rejected: free will (alone, as if Arminian liberty of indifference)

choices.english: by the force of a universal redemption
choices.why: preserve ablative of means; Redempt. abbreviated in print
rejected: universal redemption saves (drops vi / sine cognitione)
